title: STCW hours of rest: the 10, 77, 6 and 14 hour rules explained

scenes.label: STCW AND MLC
scenes.heading: Four numbers every seafarer must know
scenes.narration: Fatigue is a safety hazard, so international rules set your minimum rest. Four numbers: ten, seventy-seven, six and fourteen.

scenes.label: MINIMUM REST
scenes.heading: The two limits
scenes.narration: Under STCW and the Maritime Labour Convention, you must get at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period, and at least 77 hours in any seven-day period.

scenes.label: SPLITTING REST
scenes.heading: How rest may be divided
scenes.narration: Rest may be split into no more than two periods, and one of them must be at least 6 hours long. The gap between rest periods must not exceed 14 hours.

scenes.label: RECORDS
scenes.heading: Record it honestly, every day
scenes.narration: Drills should disturb rest as little as possible. Your daily rest hours are recorded on board, and you get a copy. Record the truth: false records hide fatigue.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: 10 in 24. 77 in 7.
scenes.narration: Remember: ten in twenty-four, seventy-seven in seven.

meta.description: The minimum hours of rest under STCW and the Maritime Labour Convention: 10 hours in any 24 hours, 77 hours in any seven days, no more than two rest periods with one of at least 6 hours, and no more than 14 hours between rest periods. Why honest rest-hour records matter.
